meta._note: What a family should check with the breeder before buying a puppy or kitten (vet feedback, David 2026-10-11). general.<species> = items for every breed; breeds.<id> = health tests of the parents. Levels: minimum = the Royal Kennel Club's 'strongly recommend that breeders, at a minimum, conduct these tests' (Good Practice) or a breeding-register requirement; best_practice = RKC Best Practice; other_scheme = an existing scheme from another A/B source that the basis page does not list. UK lists are an orientation — breeding rules in Slovenia are set per breed by the breed club under KZS (FCI Art. 19, K7). Quotes = what the fetch tool returned verbatim. Not vet-reviewed. Statuses: listed | none_recommended | not_found. general.<species>[].country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, e.g. SI) marks a national rule shown only to that country's readers; items without it apply everywhere.

quotes.quote: Make sure you see the full litter of puppies with their mother
Always make sure you see mum and her pups together
The breeder should not be willing to allow the puppies to leave their mum before 8 weeks of age.
Pedigrees, which are in fact birth certificates, must be issued for correct parentage only.
To ensure you are buying a happy and healthy puppy always ask to see the relevant health test results for both parents.
Ask to see the paperwork and check the test results and scores.
Different breeds are predisposed to different conditions so there are no blanket health test requirements.
The breeding regulations of the member countries and contract partners can go beyond those of the FCI in their requirements
The Puppy Contract, developed by the Animal Welfare Foundation and the RSPCA, will document all this information for you.
A responsible breeder should be more than happy to issue you with a contract pending the sale of one of their puppies.
